markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Industrial and Electronics show measured negative-win rates of 12.25% and 11.27%. These training-position measurements motivate investigation but do not establish validation weakness. (2) Embedding alignment near 0.51 corresponds to mean cosine near zero. It provides little justification for an anti-collapse intervention. (3) Feedback identifies specific-fit and recent-intent failures. Histories alone cannot establish ownership, compatibility, or current demand, so these remain hypotheses.

**Related work.** (1) BERT4Rec [1] prevents target leakage through masked prediction. Appended-mask inference motivates testing training examples with the same context boundary. (2) Sampled-metric analysis [2] shows that candidate sampling can change model comparisons. Consequently, auxiliary recovery results cannot replace pinned validation. (3) CAPE [3] motivates distinguishing content from position effects. Recent-history deletion alone confounds both and cannot identify causal preferences.

### Directions and framework

Three directions follow: certify execution integrity, align supervised context with inference, and measure history dependence using controlled interventions.

| Layer | Existing mechanism | Gap and proposed action |
|---|---|---|
| Integrity | Mask and padding checks | Add checkpoint/predictor parity checks |
| Learning | Bidirectional masked recovery [1] | Mix in training-prefix terminal masks |
| Explanation | History deletion | Compare position-preserving masking and random controls [3] |
| Selection | Sampled ranking [2] | Preserve host macro validation HR@10 |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Originality | Potential | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prefix terminal-mask mixture** [1] | 3: + task-specific alignment; − familiar objective | 7: + directly changes learning; − gains uncertain | 3: + sampler change; − boundary handling |
| Predictor parity certificate [1] | 3: + deployment audit; − standard testing | 6: + catches silent faults; − no direct learning improvement | 4: + bounded fixtures; − fresh-process integration |
| Position-controlled sensitivity [3] | 4: + paired controls; − established perturbations | 6: + stronger diagnosis; − no causal intent identification | 5: + existing hooks; − control construction |

### Selected idea: prefix terminal-mask mixture

At 10% progress, prioritize a small, falsifiable training change. With probability 0.5, sample a training-history endpoint, retain its preceding context, append the reserved mask, and supervise that endpoint. Otherwise retain baseline masked-target training. Both branches update the same BERT4Rec network; earlier occurrences of a repeated target remain legitimate history.

Keep architecture and scoring unchanged. Maintain left padding, final-mask readout, seeds, four-category routing, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Preserve diagnostic interfaces and record branch-specific margins with counts. Select using only host macro validation HR@10; training-prefix recovery remains explicitly training-exposed. This tests context alignment, without claiming to solve specification compatibility or infer ownership.

References: [1] BERT4Rec; [2] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation; [3] CAPE. Links and limitations accompany this report.

idea.description: Mix terminal-mask prediction on randomly selected training prefixes with the corrected baseline BERT4Rec masked-target objective, using one jointly trained network and one checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Bidirectional masked recovery can use context after a supervised position, whereas deployment predicts at an appended mask without future context. Increasing exposure to the deployment context boundary is a feasible early-stage hypothesis. Supplied training margins and qualitative feedback motivate investigation but provide no evidence that this change will improve validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: Set a fixed branch probability of 0.5 as an initial hypothesis. Sample endpoints exclusively from the supplied training histories using the existing training RNG seeded at 42. Preserve preprocessing seed 0. For a terminal example, retain at most L−1 items preceding the endpoint, append itemnum+1, and left-pad to L. Exclude the endpoint event and later events from input, while preserving legitimate earlier repeats. Compute the baseline loss only at the terminal mask for this branch; otherwise retain corrected baseline sampling and loss. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), ModelView, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics, definitions, denominators, and unavailable reasons. Maintain exactly one trained checkpoint per category, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and at most 200 epochs with 200 batches per epoch. Keep the predictor writer consistent with checkpoint configuration. Do not interpret training recovery as held-out generalization or add independently fitted scores.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in fixed_four_categories:
    initialize corrected baseline BERT4Rec with seed 42
    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            if training_rng.random() < 0.5:
                histories = sample_training_histories()
                for history in histories:
                    endpoint = sample_valid_training_endpoint(history)
                    context = history[:endpoint][-(L - 1):]
                    tokens = left_pad(context + [reserved_mask], L)
                    labels = zeros(L)
                    labels[-1] = history[endpoint]
                loss = baseline_masked_loss(model(tokens), labels)
            else:
                tokens, labels = corrected_baseline_masked_batch()
                loss = baseline_masked_loss(model(tokens), labels)
            update_same_model(loss)
    save_one_category_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()

# Diagnosis: preserve modes and RNG states; check mask construction and final
# nonpadding readout; report recovery and branch-specific margins as training-exposed.
# Selection: use only the host's fixed four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Makes an explicit, testable connection between the observed diagnostic gap and the context boundary used by deployed BERT4Rec inference.
originality.negative: Terminal-mask supervision and mixtures of masked prediction contexts are familiar techniques; no methodological novelty is established.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small controlled experiment that could clarify whether training-context alignment improves ranking within the fixed BERT4Rec family.
future_potential.negative: No validation gain is supplied, and the objective does not directly encode compatibility, ownership, or incremental usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily changes example construction while preserving the existing backbone, scorer, and predictor architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Endpoint sampling, truncation, loss masking, sampler provenance, and diagnostic label alignment require careful verification.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional sequential recommendation trained through masked-item prediction.
Provides the architectural basis for reserved-mask prediction without exposing the supervised event.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed prefix-mixture probability improves this benchmark.
Masked recovery performance alone does not establish held-out next-item ranking quality.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes distortions introduced by evaluating recommendation rankings with sampled candidates.
Supports separating auxiliary candidate-based diagnostics from the benchmark's fixed selection metric.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned host evaluator.
Repeating candidate draws does not eliminate the difference between sampled and full-catalog ranking.

related_work.title: CAPE
contributions: Studies positional encoding in attention-based sequential recommendation.
Motivates controlling positional changes when interpreting history perturbations.
limitations: Does not establish that sensitivity to recent interactions identifies causal user intent.
Does not directly validate the proposed terminal-mask training mixture.
